entries.summary: When a measurement shows a flat response across all settings of a parameter, suspect the structure being measured (global eviction across layers), not the effect: partitioning the same 51.7 GB cache per layer increased the hit rate from 23.3% to 48.0%.

Mistaken initial hypothesis that expert caching is ineffective for Kimi K3 because varying cache capacity from 512 to 4096 produced a flat 23.3% hit rate (superseded by MEM-CORR-PER-LAYER-PARTITION-002).

When varying a capacity or budget parameter across a wide range yields a completely flat metric, suspect the structure being measured (such as shared-pool cyclic eviction across stages/layers or unallocated capacity) before concluding the underlying mechanism has no effect; test partitioning the same total budget per stage/layer.
